questions.def: Sugar is uncountable, so we use 'some'.
questions.question: I need ___ sugar for my coffee.

questions.def: Milk is uncountable, so 'much' is used.
questions.question: How ___ milk do you want?

questions.def: 'Advice' is uncountable, so it doesn't have a plural form.
questions.question: Can you give me some ___ about my job?

questions.def: Water is uncountable; 'much' is used with negative uncountable nouns.
questions.question: There isn't ___ water in the bottle.

questions.def: 'Furniture' is uncountable and used with 'some'.
questions.question: She bought ___ new furniture for her house.

questions.def: Information is uncountable; it has no plural form.
questions.question: I need some ___ about the train times.

questions.def: Time is uncountable, so we use 'much'.
questions.question: Do you have ___ free time this weekend?

questions.def: Students are countable, so 'many' is correct.
questions.question: How ___ students are in the class?

questions.def: Fruit is usually uncountable in general sense.
questions.question: I ate some ___ after dinner.

questions.def: 'News' is uncountable, thus we use 'some'.
questions.question: She gave me ___ good news today.

questions.def: People are countable, therefore we use 'many'.
questions.question: There are ___ people at the party.

questions.def: 'Coffee' is uncountable, so use 'much' instead of 'many'.
questions.question: I drank too many coffee this morning, I'm jittery.

questions.def: Homework is uncountable; it doesn't have a plural form.
questions.question: I have a lot of ___ to do tonight.

questions.def: Eggs are countable; 'many' is used with countable nouns.
questions.question: We don't have ___ eggs for the cake.

questions.def: Rice is uncountable, so 'much' is correct.
questions.question: How ___ rice do you want?

questions.def: 'Cars' is plural, so use 'are' instead of 'is'.
questions.question: There is a lot of cars parked outside.

questions.def: Weather is uncountable; it doesn't have a plural form.
questions.question: The ___ today is very nice.

questions.def: Help is uncountable, so 'some' is appropriate.
questions.question: I need ___ help with my homework.

questions.def: Friends are countable, so 'many' is used.
questions.question: He doesn't have ___ friends in this city.

questions.def: Water is uncountable; the article 'a' is incorrect.
questions.question: She drinks a water every morning before work.

questions.def: Knowledge is uncountable; it has no plural form.
questions.question: He has a lot of ___ about history.

questions.def: Space is uncountable, so 'much' is used.
questions.question: There isn't ___ space in the car.

questions.def: Books are countable, therefore 'many' is correct.
questions.question: How ___ books did you buy?

questions.def: Money is uncountable; it doesn't have a plural form.
questions.question: I don't have much ___ to spend.

questions.def: Time is uncountable, so we use 'more'.
questions.question: She needs ___ time to finish the project.

questions.def: Experience is uncountable, so 'a lot of' is used.
questions.question: He has ___ experience in marketing.

questions.def: 'Some' is used with uncountable nouns in affirmative sentences.
questions.question: I need to buy ___ milk for my coffee.

questions.def: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns to ask about quantity.
questions.question: How ___ sugar do you want in your tea?

questions.def: 'Advice' is uncountable and doesn't take a plural form or article.
questions.question: Can you give me some ___ about my job?

questions.def: 'Few' is used with countable nouns like 'friends'.
questions.question: She has ___ friends in her new city.
